title.en: In, a, al, alla, nel: places and contractions

summary.en: Cities take a, rooms and regions take in, and adding 'the' fuses preposition and article into one word.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 2, and 3.

At the reception desk Chiara asks about *il viaggio in treno* to room four *al secondo piano*, Lucia explains what happened *alla stazione*, and Giulia refuses to leave a guest sad on her first evening *a* Bologna. Soon after, emergencies send the staff *in cucina* and down *in cantina*.

Use bare *a* before cities (*a* Bologna, *a* Milano) and bare *in* for countries, means of transport (*in treno*), and familiar household spaces (*in cucina*, *in cantina*, *in soffitta*). As soon as a definite article follows, *a* and *in* merge with it into one word:

| Base | + *il* | + *lo* | + `l'` | + *la* | + *i* | + *gli* | + *le* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *a* ('at / to') | *al* | *allo* | `all'` | *alla* | *ai* | *agli* | *alle* |
| *in* ('in / into') | *nel* | *nello* | `nell'` | *nella* | *nei* | *negli* | *nelle* |

On replay, compare bare *in cucina* ('in the kitchen') with contracted *nel cortile* ('in the courtyard') and *al secondo piano* ('on the second floor').
